clue.text: (& 24) For sale by the government? Premier's chief electioneers initially agree to differ!

indicators.note: the chief part of a word is its head, its first letter

parts.note: first letter

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of electioneers

parts.note: first letter

indicators.note: letters made to differ from their original order are rearranged

explanation.surface: A satirical jab at a prime minister whose electioneers agree to differ over selling honours.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye often jokes about governments trading honours for donations, hence the question mark on the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Titles in the House of Lords have repeatedly been alleged to be sold for party donations, the cash-for-honours scandal.

clue.text: One-time circus performer, Archer, reformed, cherishes independence — toe curling!

indicators.note: what one cherishes one holds close, inside one's arms
something reformed has been made into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written
I is the abbreviation for independence or independent

indicators.note: curling twists the letters out of their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Jeffrey Archer, a reformed man, prizes freedom in a cringe-making way.
explanation.walkthrough: Archer is Jeffrey Archer, the jailed novelist and Tory peer; circus here is the Roman circus, a chariot-racing arena.
explanation.definitionFit: Charioteers raced in the ancient Roman Circus, so they were performers there long ago.

clue.text: Drop off whip (little Napoleon)

parts.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip
a shortened Napoleon

explanation.surface: Someone dozes off over a whip and a short emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off is to fall asleep briefly, and a catnap is a short doze.

clue.text: (& 25) Roger has a lot of a certain carpeting

parts.note: to roger and to shag are both British slang for having sex
a pile is a large amount

explanation.surface: A man named Roger owns lots of some particular carpet.
explanation.walkthrough: Roger looks like a name but is a slang verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Shag pile is a type of carpet with a long, thick, shaggy pile.

clue.text: Awful slut, Brenda's place

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: Brenda is Private Eye's nickname for the late Queen, whose royal cipher is ER

explanation.surface: A rude Private Eye-style insult aimed at someone living in the Queen's domain.
explanation.walkthrough: Private Eye has long called Queen Elizabeth II 'Brenda'; her initials ER follow the jumbled letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ulster is a province, a region of Ireland, so it is a geographic location.

clue.text: Say, a drug session secures end of blue balls

parts.note: to utter is to say
a trip is a spell under a hallucinogen

indicators.note: 'end of' keeps only the last letter of 'blue'

parts.note: the last letter of blue

explanation.surface: A drugs session leads to an uncomfortable condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue balls' reads as a phrase, but 'end of blue' is wordplay and balls alone is the definition, meaning nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Balls is British slang for nonsense, and utter tripe means complete rubbish.

clue.text: Sod lover — certainly no heavenly bloke

parts.note: sod is turf, the earth
a woman's lover is her man

explanation.surface: An insult hurled at a lover: whatever else he is, he is no angel.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash looks like punctuation in a rant; it separates the wordplay from the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthman is a mortal of this world, so certainly not a being from the heavens.

clue.text: About the luvvy: needs to be kept stable!

parts.note: re means about or concerning
luvvy is a mocking British word for a theatrical actor

explanation.surface: A warning that a highly strung theatrical type must be kept on an even keel.
explanation.definitionFit: A nuclear reactor must be held in a stable, controlled state to avoid disaster.

clue.text: Hard to take piss in court house

indicators.note: the first pieces are placed inside the court letters
the hard letter takes the beer after it, joining them in order

parts.note: H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
piss is British slang for beer, and ale is beer

explanation.surface: A crude picture of someone finding it hard to tolerate drinking in a courtroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piss' here is slang for weak beer, not urine.
explanation.definitionFit: A chalet is a type of wooden dwelling, typically an Alpine holiday home.

clue.text: Girlfriend Cyclops is getting up — in the middle of some foliage

definitions.text: in the middle of some foliage

indicators.note: in a down entry, getting up means reading from bottom to top

parts.note: bird is British slang for a girlfriend
the setter says I am, shortened

explanation.surface: The setter is getting up to something with his girlfriend in the bushes.
explanation.definitionFit: A midrib is the central vein running down the middle of a leaf.

clue.text: (& 12/13dn./23/19) A crafty shuffling of seats — the government's typically late, pathetic response to a crisis?

definitions.meaning: literal reading: moving chairs about on a craft, a ship

definitions.text: the government's typically late, pathetic response to a crisis?
definitions.meaning: figurative reading: a pointless, cosmetic action taken while disaster looms

explanation.surface: A jibe that the government's crisis response is mere cabinet-reshuffle tinkering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crafty' looks like cunning, but it means on a craft, i.e. aboard a ship; the famous ship is the one that sank in 1912.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes futile, trivial changes made while a catastrophe is unfolding, as aboard the sinking liner.

clue.text: see 11ac.
The same thing as Dot exchanging ring with model and going without sex

indicators.note: the altered word goes outside, round the other piece
the ring-shaped letter and the Model T letter swap places in Dot

parts.note: it is a coy term for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A cheeky aside about a woman named Dot swapping her ring and model boyfriend and giving up sex.
explanation.walkthrough: The ring is the round letter, and the model is the Ford Model T; 'it' as a coy word for sex is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Ditto is used to mean likewise, signalling that an item is repeated exactly.

clue.text: see 11ac.
Nick put said modern artist in his place?

parts.note: to park something is to put it somewhere

indicators.note: said means we take the sound of the artist's name, not its spelling

parts.note: Damien Hirst, the British modern artist

explanation.surface: Someone called Nick puts an artist firmly in his place.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick is British slang for prison; Parkhurst is a prison on the Isle of Wight. 'Nick' looks like a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nick is British slang for a jail, and Parkhurst is a well-known British jail.

clue.text: Penthouse-style on-the-job situation coveted by would-be cabinet ministers?

definitions.meaning: literal reading: a workplace up at the top of a building, like a penthouse

definitions.text: situation coveted by would-be cabinet ministers?

explanation.walkthrough: Penthouse suggests the magazine and 'on-the-job' a sexual position; it just means a lofty workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: High office is an important public position, such as a cabinet post, as well as literally a lofty workroom.

clue.text: Distribution of ill-gotten gains? Very "EU" interrupting to complain

indicators.note: the inserted letters break into the middle of the other word

parts.note: to carp is to grumble or complain

explanation.surface: Someone complaining when the EU keeps butting in.
explanation.definitionFit: A carve-up is a crooked sharing out of spoils between conspirators.

clue.text: Saves Penny losing heart and holding bust out

indicators.note: the outer letters hold the other piece between them
the middle letters are lost, keeping only the ends of Penny

parts.note: its outer letters

indicators.note: out signals the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Penny, heartbroken, rescues someone while clutching a broken bust.
explanation.definitionFit: To put by money is an idiom for setting it aside and saving it for later.

clue.text: Fistful of dollars one stuffed in arse gets Cyclops a vintage car

indicators.note: things stuffed in something are packed inside it

parts.note: butt is slang for the backside
G is a grand, a thousand dollars
a means one
the setter refers to himself, I

explanation.surface: A wad of cash shoved somewhere rude buys the setter a classic car.
explanation.walkthrough: G and A go inside BUTT, and the setter's I follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Bugatti is a marque whose early models are among the most prized classic cars.

clue.text: see 11ac.
Chuck dresses down (takes balls)

parts.note: to chuck is to throw or cast
to rate someone is an old word for scolding or dressing them down

explanation.surface: Chuck tells someone off, bravely by implication.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chuck' looks like a man's name, and 'takes balls' like an idiom for courage; both are misleading.
explanation.definitionFit: To castrate is to remove the testicles, so to take away an animal's balls.

clue.text: Something for a religious arse steeped in drink to heave

definitions.note: the verb phrase with to; the answer is the bare verb

indicators.note: something steeped in liquid sits inside it

parts.note: to sup is to drink
a pew is a church bench, where a worshipper sits

explanation.surface: A drunken churchgoer feels sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Something for a religious arse' is a jokey description of a church seat, the thing a worshipper sits on.
explanation.definitionFit: To heave is to retch or vomit, which is what spew up means.

clue.text: Undergarment raised to reveal boob

parts.note: a slip is a woman's undergarment
raised means up

explanation.surface: Lifting an undergarment exposes a breast.
explanation.walkthrough: Boob looks like a breast, which suits the surface, but here it is a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A boob is British slang for a mistake, and a slip-up is a minor error.

clue.text: see 11ac.
see 1dn.
Misused by corrupt officials having endless lap dancing or other amusement with date in boozers?

definitions.note: an adjectival description standing for the money that such officials misuse

indicators.note: these pieces go inside the drinking places

parts.note: boozer is British slang for a pub

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: to lap is to lick
fun covers dancing or any amusement

explanation.surface: Bent officials spending on lap dancing and other entertainment in pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lap dancing' is not one phrase here: lap gives LIC (lick minus its end) and 'dancing or other amusement' is FUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxpayers' money is what crooked officials divert, so it is the money they misuse.

clue.text: see 4dn.
Bath, etc. overturned, revealing nuts

indicators.note: something overturned is turned upside down, so in a down entry it reads back to front

parts.note: Bath and similar towns are spa towns

explanation.surface: Toppled baths and suchlike spill out nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: Bath is the English spa city, not a tub.
explanation.definitionFit: Saps are fools or idiots, as are nuts in the sense of crazy people.

clue.text: Russia's ready to get leader of Tories out of difficulty

indicators.note: to get something out of a word is to remove it

parts.note: trouble is difficulty

indicators.note: 'leader of' keeps only the first letter of 'Tories'

parts.note: the first letter of Tories

explanation.surface: Russia is ready to help the Tory leader out of a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is not willing but readies, slang for cash; T comes out of TROUBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: The rouble is Russia's currency, and readies is slang for money.

clue.text: For those who'd have no conception of European spending limit

definitions.text: For those who'd have no conception
definitions.note: describes what the thing is for rather than naming it

parts.note: the Dutch are Europeans
a cap is an upper limit on spending

explanation.surface: European budget limits are aimed at those who have no idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No conception' seems to mean no understanding, but it means avoiding pregnancy.
explanation.definitionFit: A Dutch cap is a contraceptive diaphragm, used by people who want to avoid getting pregnant.
